name: Greenbrier

facts.what: Tender growing shoot tips and tendrils
facts.how: Raw like a bean, or cooked as an asparagus
facts.where: Woods, thickets, fence rows, often a thorny tangle

caution: Only the soft new shoot tips are food; the mature thorny vine is not. A safe, well-known trailside vegetable. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A thorny climbing vine that most people meet by snagging a shirt on it. Follow it to the soft, often reddish new growth at the tips.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Snap the tender tips off like green beans; they are crisp and mild raw and cook up like asparagus.
